result.summary: This PR removes the default-constructible, reusable PrecomputedTransactionData type in favor of construction that always ties the object to one transaction, eliminating a public Init() reuse path that could leave stale sighash cache state. It updates all call sites (validation, wallet feebumper, psbt, signet, kernel API, tests, fuzz targets) to use the new constructor or an std::optional<PrecomputedTransactionData> where construction must be deferred. As part of this, validation's ConnectBlock() and CheckInputScripts() now store txdata lazily, which also avoids allocating unused txdata during the assumevalid fast path, closing a separate previously-opened PR (#35663).
result.problem: PrecomputedTransactionData could be default-constructed and later filled with a public Init(), leaving a reuse path where an object could exist without transaction-specific data or have its internal readiness flags (notably m_spent_outputs_ready) inconsistent with what was actually cached. This is a latent correctness hazard for anyone maintaining or calling into script verification code, even though no live bug from it has been demonstrated.

resolved_concerns: sedited's design objection to the reusable Init() pattern was resolved by the author removing default construction and public Init() entirely, matching exactly what sedited proposed; no further objection was raised.

result.card: This PR makes PrecomputedTransactionData non-default-constructible so a sighash/txdata cache object can never exist half-initialized or be reused across a different transaction, removing a latent misuse hazard the author's description attributes to the old Init()-based reuse pattern. It also folds in #35663, avoiding an unnecessary txdata allocation on the assumevalid fast path in ConnectBlock. The one reviewer to comment, sedited, initially leaned NACK on the reusable-Init design; the author reworked the PR to exactly the design sedited suggested, and there has been no further review since. The PR is Ready to review: no CI failures, no rebase needed, author rebased and pinged for review as of 2026-08-05. Its importance is P3 in validation: it addresses a hazard sedited himself frames as one that 'should never' be hit in practice, so it is hardening rather than a fix for an observed bug, with a small side benefit of closing #35663's allocation-avoidance goal. It also mechanically touches kernel, wallet, and test code, which are low-priority adaptations rather than substantive changes to those areas.
